tasks.old_behavior: The strtoll() call used NULL endptr, so only errno was checked after conversion. Non-numeric tokens (e.g. 'abc') would silently produce value 0, and tokens with trailing non-numeric characters (e.g. '123abc') would silently parse the leading numeric portion and ignore the tail. The only rejected case was errno ERANGE (overflow/underflow, except for creation_time).
tasks.new_behavior: The strtoll() call now captures endptr and additionally checks: (endptr == p->tb) to detect zero-digit conversions (non-numeric input), and (endptr != p->te) to detect unconsumed trailing characters. Both cases now enter the error path and produce 'Failed to read int token.' / return NULL (unless errno==ERANGE && key==creation_time).
tasks.compatibility_reason: Config integer parsing is now stricter. Any lvm.conf, LVM metadata, profile, or command-line config string that previously happened to pass a non-integer or a value with trailing characters (e.g. whitespace due to lax formatting, stray characters, or partial migration) will now fail with 'Failed to read int token.' rather than silently producing a numeric value. This can break existing deployments that rely on the old lenient parsing, particularly during upgrades where previously-valid metadata sections or config snippets now refuse to load.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test config files with: (1) non-numeric integer keys (e.g. 'key = abc'), (2) integers with trailing non-numeric characters (e.g. 'key = 123abc'), and (3) integers with trailing whitespace depending on tokenizer behavior. All should now produce errors. Also test that well-formed integer config keys (e.g. 'key = 123') continue to work correctly, including the creation_time ERANGE special case.
